title: JSON Schema
subtitle: Validate JSON contracts and apply declared defaults
intro: Check JSON documents against a schema inside SQL, then fill missing properties from schema defaults. Useful at ingest and during audits. Invalid documents raise errors in this build, so choose strict validation or a deliberate TRY wrapper.

reference.name: json_schema_validate(schema, data)
reference.description: Return TRUE on success; raise an error on invalid data.

reference.name: json_schema_validate_schema(schema)
reference.description: Check schema acceptance; invalid schemas can raise errors.

reference.name: json_schema_patch(schema, data)
reference.description: Return JSON Patch operations for missing defaults.

reference.name: json_schema_update(schema, data)
reference.description: Return the document with defaults applied.

reference.name: TRY(expression)
reference.description: DuckDB wrapper: convert runtime validation errors into NULL.

notes.title: Make validation policy explicit
notes.body: Plain validation aborts on nonconforming input. COALESCE(TRY(json_schema_validate(...)), false) gives a filterable flag. Lint your schema first: TRY also hides malformed schemas, so a bad contract could otherwise mark every row invalid.

notes.title: Draft and defaults
notes.body: The validator primarily targets draft-07. Test the keywords your contract uses and keep reference targets within the schema. Defaults are applied by patch/update; a successful validate call alone does not rewrite the original JSON.

examples.title: Flag valid and invalid rows
examples.sql:
SELECT payload, coalesce(try(
  json_schema_validate(
    '{"type":"integer"}', payload
  )), false) AS valid
FROM (VALUES ('5'::JSON), ('"five"'::JSON))
  t(payload);
-- 5: true; "five": false
examples.caption: TRY preserves the query when a row violates the schema.

examples.title: Fill a missing property
examples.caption: The patch contains an add operation at /retries with value 3.

assertions: SELECT CASE WHEN json_schema_validate('{"type":"integer"}', '5') AND TRY(json_schema_validate('{"type":"integer"}', '"five"')) IS NULL AND (json_schema_update(getvariable('schema'), '{}')->>'retries') = '3' AND (json_schema_patch(getvariable('schema'), '{}')->>'$[0].op') = 'add' THEN true ELSE error('JSON Schema contract mismatch') END;
